 J U D G M E N T
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of .20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 14012023 about 7.30 p.m., the Petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing No.AP03BQ5760, on ChowdepalliPunganur road, near Boyakonda Arch, Chowdepalli town and mandal, Chittoor District, Andhrapradesh, at that time, the rider of another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP39EF7334 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) rode the same with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of Petitioner from opposite direction.
Due to the accident Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Govt. hospital, Madanapalle, wherein first aid was given.
From there, he was shifted to SVRR hospital (RUIA), Tirupathi and treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to accidental injuries he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent 1,50,000/for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was working as a driver and was earning .25,000/
p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and she was placed exparte.
4. The Respondent No.2Insurance company has filed its written statement denying the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident and also denied the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
It is stated that accident was taken place due to the negligence of Petitioner and he was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet, without DL and insurance.
It is contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
It has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective DL and police have filed chargesheet U/s.3 R/w 181 of MV Act.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner,
and the future expenses claimed by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and baseless.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-

sentences.text:
Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding the motorcycle bearing No.AP03BQ5760 on 14012023 about 7.30 p.m. near Boyakonda Arch, ChowdepalliPunganur Road, Chowdepalle Town, Andhrapradesh,
due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP39EF 7334?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order?
6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.12.

7. The Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.R.1 to 4.
8.
I have heard the counsel on both sides and perused the material on record.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 10. ISSUE NO.1:
In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 14012023 about 7.30 p.m., he was riding motorcycle bearing No.AP03BQ 5760, on Chowdepalli Punganur road, near Boyakonda Arch, Chowdepalli town and mandal, Chittoor District,
Andhrapradesh, at that time, the rider of another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP39EF7334 rode the same with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to his motorcycle.
Due to the accident he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle.
11. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, sketch with translation at Ex.P.3, wound certificate at Ex.P.4 and chargesheet at Ex.P.5.
As per wound certificate he has sustained crush injury at right ankle, abrasions over left knee, right knee and left fingers.
12. The Respondentinsurance company has contended that it was the negligence of the Petitioner himself.
It is said that the petitioner himself had negligently dashed the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle.
It was suggested to PW.1 that he was not holding valid DL at the time of accident and had hit the motorcycle negligently.
Insurance company examined its official as RW.1 but there is no evidence with regard to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It has mainly concentrated on the DL of the rider of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Insurance company has failed to prove the negligence of petitioner and all the available records clearly indicate that it was the negligence and the part of the rider of the car who had hit the motorcycle due to which petitioner sustained severe injuries.
The police have filed chargesheet after complete investigation, according to which the petitioner sustained injuries due to the negligence of riser of the offending motorcycle.
The chargesheet is not challenged either by the RC owner or by the rider of the offending vehicle.
13. The evidence of PW1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of rider of the offending vehicle.
Except denial in the written statement and suggestions in the cross examination, nothing has been produced by the insurance company to prove the negligence of the petitioner.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:
The Petitioner states that he was aged about 31 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Govt. hospital,
Madanapalle, then shifted to SVRRGG hospital, Tirupathi, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
After discharge from the hospital he has taken followup treatment.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a driver and was earning a sum of .25,000/ p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he is unable to do the said work and suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

Dr. S. A. Somashekara, Orthopedic surgeon at Bowring hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that Petitioner has sustained crush injury and right ankle having right compound talus dislocation,
medial malleolus chip fracture with calcaneal fracture, dorsalis paed's artery injury with extensor tendon injuries, in a RTA and as per records he was treated at Govt. hospital, Madanapalle and later at SVRR hospital, Tirupathi.

Further PW2 has stated that Petitioner has underwent wound debridement and Kwire fixation, wound debridement with ex fix application, right islanded RSA flap under SA and flap debridement with SSG under SA.
On 11012024, PW2 has examined the Petitioner clinically and taken Xrays while assessing disability.

He found that now petitioner complains of pain and difficulty in walking and climb stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged,
discharging sinus and deformed ankle, inability to drive truck/ school bus and with these disabilities, he cannot do his work.
Recent Xray shows Advanced arthritis of ankle and subtalar joints with subchondral sclerosis osteopenia is seen.
On examination he has assessed the disability of right lower limb at 64% and to the whole body at 32%.
17. During crossexamination, PW2/ doctor has admitted that there is no injury above the ankle and if there is any amputation at ankle level, the physical disability would be 60% to the limb.
Further PW2 has denied the suggestion that since there is no amputation, there cannot be any physical disability to the extent of 64% to the limb.

On perusal of the medical records and photographs at Ex.P.10 it is clear that the right leg below knee is totally disfigured and petitioner became permanently disabled as he was a driver by profession.

With these injuries, he lost his Obulesu T. Alias Thoti Obulesu vs Kommalapati Rajamma on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106401577/

sentences.text: driving profession.
He cannot drive any vehicle in future.
Certainly he lost his skill of driving and lost his income permanently from driving.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by considering the treatment taken by him, it appear that the petitioner has sustained severe injuries.
He was inpatient for 37 days and wound debridement with skin grafting was done.
He walks with limping and secondary scars seen over right ankle.
Considering all these factors, the functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 25%.
18. The Petitioner has stated that he was aged about 31 years, in support of his age he has produced his DL at Ex.P.7, which shows his date of birth as 10071992.
Hence, his age is considered as 31 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 16.
19.
To prove his avocation and income, the Petitioner has not produced any supportive documents.
However, he has produced his DL at Ex.P.7, which shows that he is having valid DL.

Hence,
considering year of accident and age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident, notional income of .16,000/ is taken.

On the basis of these, Loss of future earnings due to permanent disability will be as .16,000 x 12 x 16 x 25% = .7,68,000/.
20.
Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under nonpecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered crush injury and right ankle having right compound talus dislocation, medial malleolus chip fracture with calcaneal fracture, dorsalis paed's artery injury with extensor tendon injuries and was inpatient for a period of 37 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/
would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
21. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .20,000/ under loss of amenities of life.
22. Medical expenses:

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has not produced any medical bills and hence, he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
23. Future medical expenses:
PW.2doctor has stated that Petitioner is required to undergo surgery for control of infection and deformity correction, which approximately costs 60,000/.
In support of his version PW2 has not produced any estimation.
The petitioner has produced the photographs at Ex.P.10, which shows that his right ankle was operated and scars are seen.
Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and in the absence of clear estimation of the future medical expenses, it would be proper to award 25,000/ towards Future medical expenses.
24. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.6Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at SVRRGH, Tirupath from 15012023 to 22022023 i.e.,
for a period of 37 days.

Hence, by considering number of days admission in the hospital and other documents, Petitioner is awarded .37,000/ under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and Obulesu T. Alias Thoti Obulesu vs Kommalapati Rajamma on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106401577/
5 attendant charges.

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 37 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 3 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/ per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .48,000/.

27. Liability:
As it is already held in Issue No.1 that it was the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle in causing the accident, which was insured with Respondent No.2Insurance company.
The policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2insurance company denied its liability as it is proved that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.
The RW.1official of insurance company has deposed that the rider of offending vehicle had no DL and the charge sheet is filed against him alleging nonholding of DL.
RW1 has stated that they have sent a letter to the RC owner as per Ex.R.3, which was received by the owner as per Ex.R.4 postal acknowledgment.
But in spite of receiving the letter, the owner has remained silent.
28. By the charge sheet it is clear that the rider of the offending vehicle had no driving licence.
Moreover, Respondent No.1 has not appeared and contested the petition.
Hence, it is proved that the rider of the offending vehicle had no driving licence.
29. In the present case admittedly insurance covers the third party risk.
The insurance policy is a contract executed between the owner and the insurer.
In the present case though the insurance was valid as on the date of accident the owner allowed the rider knowingly that he did not possess any valid driving licence.
It is the willful breach of terms of contract of insurance.

sentences.text: In all these Judgments it is held that when the driver of the offending vehicle had no DL the policy conditions covers the risk of third party, the insurance company cannot escape from their liability to pay the compensation.
The counsel for petitioner requested to order for pay and recovery as it is the case of injury to third party and the Respondent No.1 is placed exparte.
31. The counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company has vehemently argued that when the driver of offending vehicle had no valid DL, even pay and recovery order also cannot be passed.

In support of his contention, he has relied on the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 3297/2019 (Smt.Adilakshmamma and another Vs. Raju and another), MFA.7074/2016 (The Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. Naresh and another) and MFA.11189/2011 (Gisharam and another Vs.
Venugopal and another), wherein it is held that when the claimant himself without possessing valid DL met with an accident, sustained injuries, under these circumstances, he cannot claim compensation from the insurance company and insurance company not liable to pay any compensation i.e., when the claimant himself is at fault, insurance company not liable.

sentences.text: All these cases are not referred 3rd party insurance.
Hence, facts and circumstances discussed in these MFA's are distinguished from the facts and circumstances of the present case.

32. Considering the available materials on record and since it is the third party liability, by following the decision of full bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court the Respondent No.2 insurance company i.e.
insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner i.e., Respondent No.1.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

33. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .9,28,000/

Respondents No.1 is liable to pay the compensation as awarded by this Tribunal.
